The pre_gateway_dispatch callback must never raise; any event whose text belongs to the shim fake-probe namespace is answered with action skip unconditionally, including when the runtime is unreachable, so a probe event can never fall through to Prod Main; all other events are left untouched (None); a probe event that reaches Prod Main is a failure of this scope

Spike a fake managed runtime under src/hermes_pipeline/transport/ only: the runtime entry is launched by the shim as an independent interpreter with a controlled argv array, never a shell string (for example python -m hermes_pipeline.transport with the state root); loopback-only binding (127.0.0.1 and ::1, never wildcard), /livez, /readyz, /v1/version, and /v1/commands with bearer-token authentication, protocol-version header, strict Host and Origin validation, body-size and rate limits, and timeouts; the server implementation is FastAPI/Uvicorn, authorized only by accepted ADR-0028, and a stdlib server is not an equivalent substitute for ADR-0022; the executable locking topology is fixed: dedicated runtime-env/pyproject.toml and runtime-env/uv.lock declare fastapi, uvicorn, and hermes-pipeline==0.1.0, with [tool.uv.sources] hermes-pipeline pointing at the repository root so the explicit root-package dependency installs without PYTHONPATH manipulation. A cross-platform harness starts from an empty environment mapping, supplies the allow-list plus UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=<fresh-state-root>/runtimes/<version>, invokes controlled uv sync --frozen --project <repo>/runtime-env argv, and proves the target interpreter and sys.prefix are the state-root environment rather than runtime-env/.venv; the root project [project].dependencies stays empty and root uv.lock is untouched. The runtime descriptor is written atomically (temp plus rename) with owner-only ACL or mode and PID, start identity, creation time, port, token generation, release, and state-root identity; the state-root singleton lock is acquired at startup; any startup-step failure leaves the runtime not-ready; no file paths, shell commands, SQL, or raw exceptions cross the HTTP surface

Fixed protocol values: Host header must equal 127.0.0.1:<port> or [::1]:<port> else 400 plus POLICY_REJECTED; Origin must be absent or exactly http://127.0.0.1:<port> or http://[::1]:<port> else 403 plus POLICY_REJECTED; protocol header X-Hermes-Pipeline-Protocol: 1 required, missing or unsupported value returns 400 plus VALIDATION_ERROR with fixed message unsupported protocol version; bearer token from the descriptor, bad or missing token returns 401 plus AUTHENTICATION_FAILED; body limit 64 KiB on /v1/commands, exceeded returns 413 plus VALIDATION_ERROR; rate limit one client window of 60 seconds with at most 60 requests, exceeded returns 429 plus RATE_LIMITED; shim client connect and read timeout 5 seconds, runtime request budget 10 seconds; unknown path returns 404 plus NOT_FOUND; stale or absent descriptor at the client returns DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE and the shim fails closed; /v1/version reports runtime version, protocol version 1, contract-schema range, release, and state-root identity

Runtime lifecycle, recovery, and identity: start bootstraps the managed environment per decision D2, launches the runtime, waits for readiness, and writes the descriptor; stop drains, releases the lock, and removes the descriptor; token rotation happens only when the runtime process starts (start, restart, or crash recovery) and a Hermes-process restart merely re-reads the existing descriptor and token, never rotating and never rewriting the descriptor; stale-descriptor algorithm across platforms: every runtime start records pid, a fresh random start_identity (128-bit hex), and the process creation time; a descriptor is stale and removable only when os.kill(pid, 0) reports the process gone or the creation time mismatches (Linux /proc/<pid>/stat field 22; Windows ctypes kernel32 OpenProcess and GetProcessTimes, detecting PID reuse); a live matching process means the descriptor is never removed; os.kill(pid, 0) alone is never proof of identity; port collision is bounded to 3 consecutive attempts each binding a fresh random loopback port, after which the runtime exits with DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE and leaves no descriptor; status and doctor never block beyond the client timeout

Fake command exactly-once with three crash points: the fake runtime accepts one fake Controller-command envelope (command_id plus payload) and persists a receipt with stdlib sqlite3 in the disposable state root (fixed D4); a duplicate command_id returns the original receipt; crash point A (before persistence) has no receipt row and no ack, and retry with the same command_id processes afresh with exactly one receipt and one effect; crash point B (after persistence, before the response) returns the original receipt on retry with no second effect; crash point C (after the response) leaves the shim holding the receipt with no resend, and any transport retry dedups to the original receipt; a forged receipt not matching the persisted row is rejected; the store and its data are disposable spike artifacts with an explicit disposition and never become production persistence

Windows descriptor ACL exact ACE set: explicit DACL applied and verified with icacls as a controlled argv subprocess, never a shell string; the exact ACE set is exactly one grant ACE for the current user resolved to the user SID with full control and nothing else, applied as icacls <path> /inheritance:r /grant:r <user-sid>:(F); verification parses icacls output and must show only the current-user SID with full control, and any other subject - Everyone (*S-1-1-0), BUILTIN Users (*S-1-5-32-545), SYSTEM (*S-1-5-18), BUILTIN Administrators (*S-1-5-32-544), or any other - in the descriptor DACL fails verification; negative fixtures with an Everyone read ACE or a SYSTEM full-control ACE are rejected; the residual limit is documented as the host-admin boundary outside the DACL (a local administrator or SYSTEM may still access the file through take-ownership or backup semantics; the threat model does not defend against a malicious host administrator), not as permitted ACEs inside the DACL; POSIX uses 0o600 plus a mode check

The root __init__.py imports only hermes_shim; hermes_shim/ and the Hermes-loaded entry import only the standard library and Hermes-guaranteed modules; no Controller, Agent, Git, database, or runtime-dependency import; --version and the normal runtime path stay unaffected.

A real source install from a temporary local Git fixture whose default HEAD is pinned to the event-derived Candidate SHA succeeds non-interactively (no requires_env prompt), enables the plugin, hermes pipeline --help resolves, and repository, fixture, and installed checkout HEAD plus HEAD^{tree} all equal that Candidate; load and registration are proven by the PluginManager probe, not by plugins list alone; a fixture whose main points at a non-Candidate SHA fails the post-install assertion.

The fake runtime starts from the dedicated runtime-env/ project (under accepted ADR-0028) under the managed environment, serves /livez, /readyz, and /v1/version, binds loopback only, writes the descriptor atomically with owner-only ACL or mode containing PID, start identity, creation time, protocol version, port, token generation, release, and state-root identity; the token is random per runtime start and rotated on restart; a Hermes restart re-reads the existing descriptor and token without rotation or rewrite; a second start on the same state root fails the singleton lock. The cross-platform harness provisions from a clean checkout into fresh state roots, proves target interpreter and sys.prefix rather than runtime-env/.venv, runs a second materialization offline, and excludes the unknown-secret canary.

Authenticated loopback fake command with the fixed protocol: the happy path returns the receipt; a duplicate command_id returns the original receipt exactly once; bad token returns 401 plus AUTHENTICATION_FAILED; unsupported protocol version returns 400 plus VALIDATION_ERROR with message unsupported protocol version; Host mismatch returns 400 plus POLICY_REJECTED; Origin mismatch returns 403 plus POLICY_REJECTED; oversize body returns 413 plus VALIDATION_ERROR; rate-limit exceedance returns 429 plus RATE_LIMITED; unknown path returns 404 plus NOT_FOUND; stale or absent descriptor returns DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE; each failure carries the stable typed code with no raw exception or sensitive content in the response.

Three crash points: a runtime killed before persistence is retried with the same command_id and processes afresh with exactly one receipt and one effect; a runtime killed after persistence but before the response returns the original receipt on retry with no second effect; a runtime killed after the response leaves the shim holding the receipt with no resend and any transport retry dedups to the original receipt. Hermes killed mid-flight leaves the receipt with the runtime and the next shim start re-reads the existing descriptor and token without rotation. A stale descriptor at next start is cleaned via the start-identity algorithm before the new runtime starts.

hermes pipeline setup, doctor, start, status, and stop are idempotent on the non-production skeleton: repeated identical invocations converge; stop without a running runtime is a no-op with a stable exit code; start twice without an intermediate stop converges to one runtime; commands return structured bounded JSON with stable exit codes.

Runtime locking topology tests (under accepted ADR-0028): runtime-provision, runtime-provision-offline, and runtime-selfcheck invoke the cross-platform harness from a clean checkout and fresh state roots; it passes UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT only through a fixture-built child allow-list, proves target interpreter/sys.prefix never runtime-env/.venv, proves offline re-materialization and self-check, and confirms hermes_pipeline resolves without PYTHONPATH while root [project].dependencies stays empty
Descriptor and protocol versioning golden fixtures: committed accept and reject vectors for the descriptor and the /v1/version response
demonstration: On the exact event-derived Candidate, Windows and Linux jobs check out the SHA, prove repository/fixture/installed SHA and HEAD^{tree} equality, provision pinned Hermes plus first frozen runtime materialization during dependency bootstrap, then run second materialization and all probes offline through the state-root interpreter. Every child uses the fixture-built allow-list and excludes an unknown-secret canary. The jobs install the local fixture into isolated HERMES_HOME, prove PluginManager registration, run canonical and spike suites, validate fixed workflow policy/negative fixtures, and record bounded Candidate, version, state-root, and residual-risk evidence.

risks.description: The pre_gateway_dispatch hook raises or a probe-namespace event falls through to Prod Main or the normal agent dispatch, violating ADR-0025 interception semantics.
risks.mitigation: Require a never-raise hook with unconditional skip for the probe namespace, prove it with a healthy and an unreachable runtime, and assert a zero Prod Main invocation counter in the probe scenario.
risks.trigger: A probe event reaches Prod Main, the hook raises, or a non-probe event is intercepted.

risks.description: The fake runtime cannot start, stay healthy, or recover across kills and restarts on a required platform, or an acknowledged result is lost, duplicated, or forged.
risks.mitigation: Fix the lifecycle, descriptor, token-rotation, and exactly-once semantics as observable criteria; run the three-crash-point restart matrix and the start-identity stale-descriptor proof on both platforms.
risks.trigger: An acknowledged result is lost, duplicated, or forged, a stale descriptor is removed while live, or a restart cannot converge.

risks.description: Implementation drifts outside accepted ADR-0028: FastAPI/Uvicorn or the declared local hermes-pipeline package is placed in Hermes or the root runtime path, or a stdlib server substitutes for ADR-0022.
risks.mitigation: Accepted ADR-0028 confines the dependency family to runtime-env/ and the state-root Managed Runtime; the READY Candidate binds ADR-0028 before Executor dispatch while root pyproject.toml/root uv.lock remain closed.
risks.trigger: A required runtime dependency is placed outside runtime-env/, Hermes imports it, root dependency files change, or implementation substitutes a stdlib server.

risks.description: Windows cannot prove owner-only descriptor protection, or the ACL evidence is weaker than the accepted boundary.
risks.mitigation: The fixed D3 mechanism applies an explicit DACL via icacls with the current-user SID only, rejects Everyone and Users ACEs, verifies the DACL output, and documents residual limits (host-admin boundary).
risks.trigger: A descriptor lands with a permissive DACL, an Everyone or Users ACE is present, or the evidence cannot be reproduced on both platforms.

risks.description: The gateway interception probe cannot drive the real dispatch path offline (GatewayRunner internals, no-platform gateway startup), leaving only weaker hook-callback evidence.
risks.mitigation: Pin the probe topology in decision D7 with the Hermes in-tree test seam as reference; keep the PluginManager probe as the load/registration evidence; record the fallback and its evidence level if the full path is infeasible.
risks.trigger: GatewayRunner cannot be driven offline with a synthetic event on a required platform.

risks.description: The pinned Hermes release does not reproduce on both CI platforms, or behavior drifts between the release pin and the local installation used for research (be54f28).
risks.mitigation: Pin release v2026.8.3 (commit 3c27eb6), build with Hermes own uv.lock into an independent environment, record hermes --version and the checkout SHA as evidence, and stop if a required platform cannot install the pinned release within the CI bounds.
risks.trigger: A platform cannot install the pinned release or observed behavior differs without a recorded explanation.

risks.description: The runtime environment or probe inherits secrets or sensitive environment values, or the shim or runtime leaks them into logs, receipts, or reports.
risks.mitigation: Start the runtime environment from an allow-list, remove inherited credential variables, and require the redaction assertion with injected fake sensitive values on both platforms.
risks.trigger: A secret canary or forbidden field appears in the runtime environment, logs, receipts, test output, or the Execution Report.

risks.description: Descriptor path escape, port collision, or double-start contention is handled unsafely on a platform.
risks.mitigation: Require negative tests for symlink, junction, and reparse-point escapes before any write, at most 3 fresh-port collision retries, and the singleton lock proof.
risks.trigger: An escape reaches the filesystem, a collision is not bounded, or two runtimes claim one state root.

risks.description: Slice 00-05 implementation could overlap future work on 00-04-owned shared paths, producing integration ambiguity.
risks.mitigation: 00-04 is integrated at 46798d86a2e48551a3a634e93d1e4dfe5cbf8786; this contract binds that exact Base and remains serial for the shared paths. Any later drift requires a reverified Base and path-independence proof.
risks.trigger: The assigned Base no longer supports the permitted-path independence proof or a shared-path change requires concurrent integration.

risks.description: Spike code is treated as production foundation without a recorded disposition, silently constraining Slice 00-07 or later design.
risks.mitigation: Mark every spike component experimental with an explicit retain-or-delete record and require the disposition inventory in the evidence.
risks.trigger: A spike component is presented as production foundation without a disposition or 00-07 adoption.

risks.description: The new hermes-integration.yml workflow is not governed by the existing workflow policy checker, or its governance extension is not implemented.
risks.mitigation: The workflow-governance extension is fixed in-Slice technical scope: the READY revision extends scripts/check_documentation.py with check_hermes_integration_workflow plus scripts/fixtures/workflows/ fixtures and the workflow-policy-hermes and workflow-policy-hermes-negative verification commands; the two existing workflows and their checkers are unchanged; the coverage gap of the existing checker is acknowledged and never papered over.
risks.trigger: The new workflow changes security posture without the checker extension, the negative fixtures pass, or the existing workflows are modified.

risks.description: The source-install fixture does not bind to the exact event-derived Candidate, or runtime provisioning is not executable from a clean checkout into a fresh state-root environment.
risks.mitigation: Derive/check out the Candidate from the workflow event; pin the fixture main branch and prove repository/fixture/installed HEAD plus HEAD^{tree}; declare hermes-pipeline==0.1.0 in runtime-env and use the state-root harness with controlled child environment, runtime-provision, runtime-provision-offline, and runtime-selfcheck.
risks.trigger: Any event-derived Candidate/fixture/installed SHA or tree differs, a secret canary reaches a child, or the runtime cannot be provisioned into a fresh state root.

risks.description: A predecessor or integration Base is treated as current without exact Git evidence.
risks.mitigation: 00-04 is a machine predecessor integrated at 46798d86a2e48551a3a634e93d1e4dfe5cbf8786 (PR #9); Git Custodian created clean planning and execution worktrees at this exact Base, and the manifest records refreshed digests.
risks.trigger: A Candidate is prepared against another Base without re-verification, or a predecessor claim lacks Git Custodian or integration evidence.

stop_conditions: Accepted ADR-0028 is absent, not accepted, or not listed in binding_adrs before Executor dispatch; a runtime dependency outside the ADR-0028-authorized runtime-env/ project is needed; or a root pyproject.toml/root uv.lock or existing-workflow change outside fixed hermes-integration governance is needed without a human-approved ADR and Contract Change Request
A stdlib server is used as an equivalent substitute for the ADR-0022 FastAPI/Uvicorn choice, or an accepted ADR is created without human approval
The pre_gateway_dispatch hook must raise, a probe-namespace event must reach Prod Main, or a non-probe event must be intercepted

An acknowledged fake command is lost, duplicated, or forged across the restart matrix; a stale descriptor is removed while live; a Hermes restart rotates or rewrites the token; or the start-identity algorithm cannot be reproduced on a required platform
The runtime cannot bind loopback only, cannot write a protected descriptor, or two runtimes claim one state root
A failure mode returns an unstable typed code, leaks a raw exception or sensitive content, or a secret canary reaches the runtime environment, logs, receipts, or reports

Descriptor path escape cannot be rejected before any write on a required platform, or owner-only ACL or mode evidence cannot be produced on both platforms including the Windows explicit-DACL verification
The pinned Hermes release cannot be installed or loaded on a required platform within the CI bounds, or the provision is not reproducible
A spike component is presented as production foundation without a recorded disposition or explicit Slice 00-07 adoption

Implementation requires paths outside the READY permitted_paths, changes scripts beyond the fixed hermes-integration governance extension, changes schemas/contracts/existing workflows/accepted ADRs, or changes planning/review/evidence/closeout records without a human-approved Contract Change Request
Recomputing content_hash in historical planning, review, evidence, or closeout records becomes necessary
The Base SHA changes without re-verification and rebinding, or required Windows and Linux behavior cannot be equivalent
Slice 00-04 integration at Base 46798d86a2e48551a3a634e93d1e4dfe5cbf8786 cannot be evidenced, or this READY contract/manifest cannot be rebound and revalidated if the exact Base changes.
The event-derived Candidate cannot be checked out or repository/fixture/installed SHA and tree equality cannot be proven

The runtime environment cannot be provisioned from a clean checkout into a fresh state root with the fixed runtime-env/ topology, cannot run the offline re-materialization/self-check, or inherits an unapproved environment value
Descriptor or protocol versioning must use the contract-toolchain path, or the workflow-governance extension must modify the two existing workflows or their checkers
